    • getRetrievalTimeout

      public @NonNull Duration getRetrievalTimeout()
      Description copied from interface: JwksClientConfiguration
      How long a remote JWK Set retrieval may take before it is given up and treated as a failure. It bounds the retrieval shared by concurrent callers even when the underlying JwksClient has no timeout of its own. A zero or negative duration disables the timeout.
      Specified by:
      getRetrievalTimeout in interface JwksClientConfiguration
      Returns:
      The retrieval timeout.

    • setRetrievalTimeout

      public void setRetrievalTimeout(@NonNull Duration retrievalTimeout)
      How long a remote JWK Set retrieval may take before it is given up and treated as a failure, which starts the failure back-off. Concurrent callers share one retrieval per signature configuration and url, so without this timeout a retrieval which never completes (for example a JWKS client without timeouts of its own) would block every token for that configuration. Set it to 0 to disable the timeout. Default value (30 seconds).
      Parameters:
      retrievalTimeout - The retrieval timeout.

    • setFailureBackoff

      public void setFailureBackoff(@NonNull Duration failureBackoff)
      How long a remote JWK Set is not requested again after a retrieval failed (for example, connection refused, non-2xx response or unparseable body) or returned no keys. While the back-off lasts, tokens which cannot be verified with another signature configuration are rejected without contacting the JWKS endpoint again. Set it to 0 to disable the back-off. Default value (10 seconds).
      Parameters:
      failureBackoff - The failure back-off duration.
